label: GO after an unrewarded trial, late in the episode (a1 / reward-drought)
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass; never at D1 or D2), and almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward==0 has 99.8% of mass, recall 0.99, but precision 0.11). Strongly gated by how far into the episode it is: zero before trial ~20, and the rate rises steadily to its maximum at trials 90-99 (ep_trial>=50 has 98.6% of mass). Within that, it is stronger and more likely when there has been a run of unrewarded trials (the previous trial also unrewarded), when the model is choosing a1 (82% of mass; policy logit strongly favours a1), and when the model value is low (no activations in the top value bin). The recorded predicate uses only observed variables plus the agent own current choice (model_act at GO): GO & prev unrewarded & ep_trial>=60 & (two unrewarded trials in a row OR choosing a1). The simpler GO & prev_reward==0 & ep_trial>=70 gets dev F1 0.43 with mass recall 0.87; the recorded one gets dev F1 0.53 with mass recall 0.92. Precision stays low (~0.39), so many late unrewarded GO steps stay silent. Its magnitude probably tracks a graded variable like elapsed time or reward-drought (value), which no boolean captures. Not driven by transition type or the hidden good state, apart from the a1 / S1-good correlation.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a1 S2 u, a2 S2 u, ?) and trial before (GO: a1 S1 u, a1 S2 u, a2 S2 u); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=9, phase=GO & ep_dec=8, phase=GO & ep_dec=7.
